headline: Wet, breezy week ahead, with coastal flooding and gales likely and more systems through Thanksgiving.
summary: A cold upper-level low parked offshore keeps showers over western Washington tonight. A dip in the high-altitude winds arriving Monday sends a string of storms our way through the week. Monday and Tuesday bring widespread rain and gusty southeast winds, strongest on the coast. The wettest stretch looks like Wednesday into Thursday, when the Skokomish River may near flood stage and the Grays Harbor coast could see flooding. Gales and high surf are likely into the holiday, with a brief break by Friday. Forecasters are fairly confident in a wet, windy week, but unsure how strong the midweek low will be, since its exact path matters.
changes: Coastal flooding risk moved up: a flood warning now covers Monday morning's high tide on the Grays Harbor coast, where earlier discussions had only advisories. The latest discussion also adds a brief break in the winds by Friday.
